title: metais.schema/1
description: What metais schema prints with --json: the combined input schema, or one input's schema as a self-contained Compound Schema Document (ADR-008 D5, schema); or, with --fields, the compact field listing in the schema's place (ADR-008 A7).

input.description: The input's name, or null for the combined schema.

schema.description: The schema, a JSON Schema 2020-12 document, its members in canonical key order.

fields-result.description: With --fields: one entry per field, in the order the text listing prints them (ADR-008 A7).

input.description: The input's name, or null for every input's fields.

field.description: One declaration of a field: what the schemas that declare it at its pointer, under its conditions, say of its value.

pointer.description: The field's JSON Pointer, its first token the input's name, as --set takes it; the token * stands for every element of an array, or every member of an object its schema does not name.

type.description: The declared type names, in the order type gives them; empty when no declaring schema names a type.

required.description: Whether an object declaring the field, under the field's conditions, requires it.

constraints.description: Each assertion and default the declaring schemas make, as keyword=<canonical JSON>, in their order; name-matches=<JSON string> for a member patternProperties selects; false for a false schema; a value longer than 1024 bytes is cut on a character boundary and ends […+N bytes; <command> prints it whole], and a last entry […; <command> prints every constraint] says the line's constraints were cut at 4096 bytes; <command> is metais schema <package> <input>, or metais schema <package> for the combined listing, which prints the schema whole.

title.description: The first title of the declaring schemas, cut as a constraint is, or null.

when.description: The conditions the declaration applies under, outermost first; empty when it always applies.

same_as.description: The pointer where the fields beneath a schema that also declares this field were listed, or null.

beyond_value_depth.description: True when fields beneath this one are declared and not listed, since they lie deeper than value-depth beneath the input.
